Quick technical readout (initial hypothesis):

On Wed, May 18, 2026 at 4:43 PM Alex Gomez <agomez@crimsoncore.com> wrote:
> We flipped CrimsonCore to your new quant-profile v2.1 last night...

What we’re seeing in the traces and internal perf counters:
- The v2.1 qprofile increases per-token compute for long-context attention kernels due to a tighter int8 packing layout; for the hot route that often sends 1.2–1.6k tokens, this increases kernel invocation latency.
- More importantly, v2.1 changes the KV cache slice boundaries which causes a higher rate of cache rehydration across shards under our continuous-batching policy. That triggers extra RPCs and amplifies tail latency under bursty traffic.
- Error spike (5xx) likely due to temporary OOM/slow-paths on a small subset of hosts where the new kernel path hits a path with reduced memory headroom.

Mitigations we can apply now (one or more):
1) Per-tenant pin: revert CrimsonCore to qprofile v2.0 (fastest, lowest risk) — ETA ~45–70m if agreed.
2) Hotfix: temporarily disable continuous-batching for CrimsonCore’s route (reduces KV rehydration at cost of some throughput). ETA ~20–30m.
3) Config: force FP16 path for CrimsonCore to avoid int8 kernel variability (requires restart of 2 nodes). ETA ~25–40m.

I recommend: immediate hotfix to disable continuous-batching so their user-facing latency improves within 30m; then plan a rollback to v2.0 if tail does not recover. I’ll prepare a minimal RCA and the perf counters snapshot for the bridge.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime
